name: Axiom Systems Biometric Lock Rifle BLR-3 'Personal'
description: A bullpup assault rifle with an integrated biometric lock system that prevents anyone other than the registered owner from firing it. The BLR-3 reads the operator's palmprint, pulse pattern, and neural interface signature simultaneously — all three must match the registered profile or the trigger mechanism remains physically locked. Axiom developed it to prevent weapon capture and misuse during corporate conflict, ensuring that seized weapons cannot be turned against their issuing force. The biometric system has been praised as a safety innovation and condemned as a control mechanism — operators cannot share weapons with allies, cannot use captured enemy BLR-3s, and cannot sell or transfer the weapon without an Axiom technician re-registering it.
specifications: caliber: 5.56mm caseless magazine: 40 rounds rate of fire: 750 RPM effective range: 50-400 meters biometric lock: Palmprint + pulse + neural interface triple authentication authentication time: 0.3 seconds on grip weight: 3.5 kg fire modes: Semi, burst, full auto re-registration: Requires Axiom technician
story_hooks: A dead Axiom operative's BLR-3 was fired after their death — the biometric system accepted a dead hand, dead pulse, and a cloned neural interface signature, meaning someone duplicated the operator's entire biometric profile.

A firmware exploit allows BLR-3 rifles to be permanently unlocked by injecting a specific code through the maintenance port — the exploit is spreading through underground channels and Axiom cannot patch it remotely.
image_prompt: Product photography of the Axiom Systems BLR-3 bullpup rifle lying diagonally across a matte black carbon fiber surface. Dramatic side-lighting (40-degree angle) creates sharp shadows emphasizing the angular grip module and sensor ring. The biometric sensor array glows softly with amber LEDs indicating 'ready to authenticate.' Close-up focus on the circular grip section showing the polished aluminum sensor ring with visible micro-texturing and translucent sensor windows. The rifle's gunmetal gray polymer body recedes into shadow, while the grip becomes the focal point—clinical, precise, almost medical in appearance. Shallow depth of field. High-contrast neo-noir urban aesthetic with cool color grading (blue-gray tones). In the blurred background, faint Axiom Systems corporate branding. No human hands visible—the weapon sits as an autonomous object, its biometric sensors somehow aware and waiting. --ar 3:2 --v 6

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact bullpup rifle with an aggressive, almost skeletal aesthetic. The weapon's frame appears almost utilitarian—stripped of ornament—with a pronounced angular grip that juts forward beneath the receiver. The biometric sensor array around the grip is unmistakable: a ring of brushed metallic contacts and translucent sensor windows that glow faintly when powered. The overall silhouette reads as deliberately uncomfortable to hold by unauthorized hands.
physical_description.dimensions: 640mm length, 190mm width (at magazine), 95mm height. Barrel: 310mm. Compact and optimized for close-quarters corporate environment deployment.
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and balanced, 3.5kg feels almost delicate in trained hands—designed for extended wear on security rotations. The weight distribution tips slightly toward the grip module due to biometric hardware concentration, creating an odd sense of the weapon 'pointing' toward its owner's body.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite core (DuPont Kevlar-infused) with embedded steel reinforcement along the receiver and barrel. The biometric grip section uses aerospace-grade aluminum alloy with integrated circuit traces visible beneath translucent polymer caps.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray polymer with brushed aluminum accents. The grip ring features a subtle iridescent sheen from the optical sensors beneath the surface. Wear areas show bare aluminum where operators' gloved hands contact repeatedly.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray body with polished chrome biometric sensor ring. Axiom's corporate crimson accent stripe runs along the top rail. Dark polymers dominate; the metallic grip assembly stands out as the weapon's 'eye'—clinical and observant.
physical_description.grip_texture: The grip itself features aggressive microtexture—almost like shark skin—designed to reject sweat and ensure consistent palmprint contact with sensor pads. Cool to the touch, slightly grippy. The biometric ring is smooth polished aluminum with subtle tactile alignment notches for finger positioning.
distinctive_features: Circular biometric sensor ring around the grip module with visible sapphire-crystal sensor windows
Three nested LED indicator zones (green/amber/red) on the grip frame showing authentication status
Integrated pulse-pattern sensor pads embedded in grip surfaces—visible as burnished metal rectangles
Neural interface sync port (USB-C equivalent) recessed into the receiver, sealed with a red polymer cap
Dual-stage trigger mechanism with a secondary 'lock pin' visible when disassembled
Heat signature identification vents (small rectangular ports) above the magazine well
Axiom Systems corporate serial plate mounted at 45-degree angle on receiver, with individual biometric profile hash laser-etched beneath
Wear marks on the grip ring where thousands of authentication cycles have burnished the aluminum
Battle-scarred polymer body typical of Tier-3 security forces—small impact marks, scuff patterns, but biometric surfaces kept pristine
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Axiom Systems crimson logo (corporate shield with stylized Φ currency symbol) positioned on the left receiver. Serial plate mounted asymmetrically on the lower right receiver. Biometric profile hash code etched in white text on the serial plate. Small 'AXIOM REGISTERED WEAPON' warning label in English/Mandarin/Hindi on grip ring.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. The biometric surfaces are always cleaned—authentication failure due to contamination is unforgivable in corporate environments. The polymer body shows consistent cosmetic damage: scuffs, stress marks at stress points, but the weapon functions perfectly. Some weapons show personalized enhancements: grip tape additions, sight upgrades, custom rail covers—modifications that don't interfere with the biometric lock's operation.
